measurements.statement: exactly twelve hummingbirds distributed from top edge to bottom edge and left edge to right edge

measurements.how_measured: visually estimated share of frame covered by painted birds, leaves, nest and sky wash versus blank paper
measurements.statement: about 95% of the frame is filled image with full bleed; subjects touch all four edges leaving no margins

measurements.how_measured: compared area of green plumage versus red-orange-red crests, throats and tails across all birds
measurements.statement: green is present on all twelve birds covering about half the frame; warm red-orange accents appear on about ten birds covering about 15% of the frame

measurements.how_measured: divided frame horizontally by background tone from pale upper left to dark lower right
measurements.statement: top third is pale blue-white sky while bottom two-thirds is dark brown-green foliage, with light-to-dark transition near the middle

measurements.how_measured: traced long axes of bodies, beaks and tails in the central band
measurements.statement: at least eight birds point on crossing diagonals northeast-southwest versus northwest-southeast, intersecting in the center third

measurements.how_measured: compared longest body-plus-tail extent of bottom bird to smallest top-left bird relative to frame height
measurements.statement: largest bird length is about one-third of frame height, smallest about one-sixth, a ratio of about 2 to 1 with overlapping wings and tails

hypotheses.statement: Abundance and variety feel comes from packing many similarly-sized colorful subjects edge-to-edge with a shared dominant color so the eye reads plenty without chaos.
Depth and downward flow work because the pale open sky in the upper third gives way to dark dense foliage in the lower two-thirds, moving the eye from airy flight to sheltered perching.
Liveliness and tension hold without a single focal point because bodies, beaks and tails form opposing diagonals that cross in the center and repeat at similar scale.

relations.rule: Fill the canvas edge-to-edge with subjects so coverage stays above 90% with no margins or isolated white space.
Keep one dominant hue on every subject and restrict warm accent hues to small patches totaling 10-20% of the frame.
Alternate subject axes on opposing diagonals so long forms cross near the center to create continuous movement without a single focal point.

fragile_if_changed: Isolating the birds with empty background or margins would destroy the dense, overlapping cabinet-of-curiosities abundance that defines its character.

skin_measured.how_measured: k-means (6 clusters) on the sent pixels for bg/fg; accent = median of strongly saturated mid-lightness pixels (s>0.45, 0.2<l<0.8) inside region 'green plumage with red-orange accents'
